input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: § 7.2 is a reverse MFN running against us: it obliges Customer to disclose any more favourable third-party commercial offer and match it for Vendor, with no product scope, time limit, or comparison carve-outs. That is the walk-away position (open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor) and it contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN in our favour exists elsewhere, so deletion of p0026 is the minimal fix; the fallback (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) is offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the reverse most-favoured-nation obligation in § 7.2, as our playbook does not permit us to disclose or match third-party offers for Vendor's benefit; this also aligns with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have given no most-favoured-customer commitment. If Vendor needs something here, we could consider a narrow MFN limited to a defined product for 12 months with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
